name: Dravanet Pecs Data Center
notes: DataCenterMap lists one data center in Pecs, Baranya, operated by Dravanet Zrt. at Budai Nagy Antal u. 1, 7624 Pecs; ColoMap separately describes Dravanet Pecs as a colocation data center at the same address. No public MW figure found.

name: Magyar Telekom Cloud & DataCenter Budapest / Dataplex
notes: Magyar Telekom's wholesale hosting page lists T-Systems Cloud & DataCenter at 1087 Budapest, Asztalos Sandor u. 13. Telekom Wholesale describes the Budapest facility as one of the region's highest-tech data centers; third-party listings identify it as Dataplex, established in 1999 with 8,800 sqm technical space. Baxtel market summary reports Dataplex as Hungary's largest data center with 8 MW.

name: Invitech DC10 Adatkozpont
notes: DatacenterPlatform lists Invitech DC10 at Kozma u. 2, 1108 Budapest. Inflect reports 2,000 kW power capacity. Uptime Institute lists Invitech Solutions DC10-III in Budapest, Hungary. 2Connect, formed from Antenna Hungaria, DIGI infrastructure, Invitech and Vodafone Hungary network units, says it operates more than 6,500 sqm of data center capacity across 12 sites.

name: VIVAnet DC Budapest
notes: VIVAnet's official site states that VIVAnet DC is a carrier-neutral data center in the heart of Budapest, operating since July 2024, with first-phase room capacity for 140 rack cabinets. No public MW figure found.

name: Wigner Data Center for CERN
developer: Wigner Research Centre for Physics / CERN
notes: CERN and Wigner inaugurated the Budapest extension to CERN's data centre on 2013-06-13, with about 500 servers, 20,000 computing cores and 5.5 PB storage already operational. CERN Courier reported the 2012 contract for Wigner to host CERN equipment extending Tier-0 Worldwide LHC Computing Grid capability. MW not disclosed in public source.

name: Magyar Telekom Victor Hugo DC
notes: Magyar Telekom's wholesale hosting pages list Victor Hugo DC at 1132 Budapest, Victor Hugo 18-22 among its data centers. Baxtel also lists Magyar: Victor Hugo DC as a Budapest facility. Capacity not publicly disclosed.

name: Rackhost Data Center Budapest / Victor Hugo
notes: Rendszerinformatika's official Victor Hugo datacenter page lists 1132 Budapest, Victor Hugo street 18-22, 70 rack spaces, 270 sqm gross area and 3 kW per rack. Capacity estimate is 70 racks x 3 kW = 210 kW / 0.21 MW. DataCenterMap lists Rackhost Data Center Budapest at the same Victor Hugo address.

name: University of Miskolc Supercomputer
notes: Daily News Hungary/MTI reported that the University of Miskolc inaugurated an EU-funded supercomputer on 2015-10-13. This is an institutional HPC facility rather than a commercial colocation site; public sources did not disclose MW. University pages identify the campus IT centre but not detailed datacenter specs.

name: Magyar Telekom Adatpark Szeged
notes: Magyar Telekom's official wholesale hosting pages list Adatpark Szeged at 6724 Szeged, Rokusi krt. 2-10. DataCenterMap and Baxtel list Magyar Telekom Adatpark Szeged as an operational data center. No public MW figure found.

name: Rackhost Data Center Szeged
notes: DataCenterMap's Szeged page and nearby-facility listing identify Rackhost Data Center Szeged at Tisza Lajos krt. 41. Rackhost's company page lists two data centers in two markets, consistent with Budapest and Szeged. No public MW figure found.

name: Komondor Supercomputer Center at University of Debrecen
notes: University of Debrecen reported that KIFU's 5-petaflop Komondor supercomputer was installed at UD's Kassai Street campus and put in service after testing. The HPC page says Komondor was installed in the national HPC centre on the Kassai campus in summer 2023 and lists maximum electrical power of 500 kW.
